<reason>CON built the cleaner path to victory on targeting and control: fines bill the named public-facing service after lockout, often a locked agency that cannot rewrite vendor code, while buying checklist patches rather than completed tasks. PRO’s 20-year voluntary-failure story and “who forces the procurement clause” pressure were real, but they never displaced CON’s claim that the motion’s instrument is systematically misaimed. PRO’s clipped opening and the mid-debate slide toward task-completion fines (then a walk-back) also left CON with the easier vote on the motion as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s first rebuttal recast PRO’s alleged contradiction as one instrument failing twice, then Pressure Q2 plus PRO’s “yes, still fine them” turned repeated failure after a grace period into a surcharge on incapacity rather than proof of refusal.</best_rebuttal>
